report_name: Hacker Group Claims Breach of Brazilian University, Affecting 53,000

threat_actors.name: BLCKORDER
threat_actors.description: A threat actor group that claimed responsibility for a data breach against Celso Lisboa University, advertising the stolen data on a dark web forum.
threat_actors.goals: Sale of stolen personal data for financial profit.

threat_actors.name: Duk3nk
threat_actors.description: The user alias on a dark web forum who advertised the Celso Lisboa University database for sale on behalf of the BLCKORDER group.

identities.name: Celso Lisboa University
identities.description: A higher education institution in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, allegedly breached by the BLCKORDER threat actor group, with data of 51,000 students and 2,000 employees offered for sale.

infrastructure.name: Dark Web Criminal Forum
infrastructure.description: A dark web forum used by the threat actor 'Duk3nk' to advertise and sell the database allegedly stolen from Celso Lisboa University.

indicators.name: Anomalous Student Information System (SIS) Access
indicators.pattern:
title: Anomalous Student Information System (SIS) Access
id: 2b8a1c9d-4f5e-4b6c-8d9a-0e1f2a3b4c5d
status: experimental
description: >
  Detects potentially anomalous access to a Student Information System (SIS) database. This is a hunting rule to look for broad queries that could be part of a data theft attempt. True detection of high-volume queries often requires SIEM correlation logic.
references:
  - https://www.bitsight.com/underground/data-breaches
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-11-15
tags:
  - attack.t1213
level: low
logsource:
  category: database
detection:
  selection:
    statement|re: '(?i)SELECT .* FROM .*(student|user|employee|person).*'
  filter:
    user:
      - 'backup_user'
      - 'reporting_service'
  condition: selection and not filter
indicators.description: Monitors for anomalous access to Student Information System (SIS) databases, such as a single account querying thousands of student records in a short period, which could indicate data theft.

indicators.name: Anomalous Large Data Transfer from SIS Server
indicators.pattern:
title: Anomalous Large Data Transfer from SIS Server
id: 8c9d0e1f-2a3b-4c5d-6e7f-8a9b0c1d2e3f
status: experimental
description: >
  Detects a large volume of outbound data from a known Student Information System (SIS) server, which could indicate data exfiltration. Thresholds should be tuned for the specific environment.
references:
  - https://www.bitsight.com/underground/data-breaches
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-11-15
tags:
  - attack.t1041
level: medium
logsource:
  category: firewall
detection:
  selection:
    src_ip: 
      - 192.168.1.10 # Placeholder for SIS server IP
    bytes_out|gt: 100000000 # Example: > 100MB
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Looks for a Student Information System (SIS) server sending an unusually large amount of data to an unknown internal or external IP address, suggesting data exfiltration.

indicators.name: Dormant Account Logon
indicators.pattern:
title: Dormant Account Logon
id: 4f5e6a7b-8c9d-4e0f-1a2b-3c4d5e6f7a8b
status: experimental
description: >
  Detects a logon from an account that has been inactive for a long period (e.g., > 90 days). This is a common TTP as attackers often use compromised, forgotten accounts to blend in. This rule is conceptual and requires a SIEM capable of tracking last logon times.
references:
  - https://www.bitsight.com/underground/data-breaches
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-11-15
tags:
  - attack.t1078
level: medium
logsource:
  category: authentication
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    EventID: 4624
    # This logic is conceptual and depends on the SIEM's ability to enrich events with user account age or last logon data.
    # For example, a field like 'user_days_since_last_logon' > 90
  condition: selection
indicators.description: Alerts on logins from accounts that have been inactive for a long period, as these are often compromised and used by attackers for initial access or lateral movement.

relationships.source_name: Anomalous Large Data Transfer from SIS Server
